# Design decisions and the principle behind them {#sec-principled-decisions}

**Every architectural decision in ISLA was made by one rule: an accuracy
gain is not accepted when it is known to come from a violation of a
physical principle.** A surrogate for a boundary-value problem should depend
on the geometry, the boundary conditions and the physics, and on nothing
else. When a change improves the score by reading the mesher's cell pattern,
the sampling density, or a statistic of the drawn sample, the improvement is
a fit to the discretization, and it will not survive a different mesher, a
different sampling law, or a geometry the training set did not contain. This
appendix is the ledger of every decision of that kind: the alternative it
rejected, what the alternative would have bought on the in-distribution
metric, what it consumed that the physics does not provide, and the evidence.
It exists so that the paper on ISLA can say *why* the architecture is what it
is, and so that the position is stated plainly for others: a program that
wants highly generalizable physics surrogates has to be willing to leave
measured accuracy on the table when that accuracy is known to be
non-physical.^[Not everything that is measured counts, and not everything
that counts can be measured. The aphorism is William Bruce Cameron's
(*Informal Sociology*, 1963); it is often misattributed to Einstein.]

## The criterion, and how it was audited {#sec-principled-criterion}

The operational form of the principle is **consistency in the fine-mesh
limit** (@sec-principle). Under uniform refinement of the sampled boundary
the prediction must converge to one field, and under two different sampling
laws of the same surface it must converge to the same field; a dependence on
the sampling distribution that does not vanish with refinement is a defect,
however much it improves a score at a fixed cell count. A falling error with
more cells is not a defect. A different answer under a different sampler at
every count is. The test that decides is therefore never a single accuracy
number: it is the consistency benchmark of @sec-consistency-bench, which
scores every model under three samplers at four cell counts.

Two questions were asked of every proposed change, before and after it was
measured. *Why should this work*, in mechanistic terms? And would a
practitioner of classical CFD look at the construction without objecting to
what it consumes? Changes that could not answer both were run, when they
were run at all, as ablations, and are labelled so wherever they appear.
Past changes were audited by the same two questions after the rule was
written (@sec-nb-principle-redirect), and two were reversed as a result: a
rule that would have adopted the weights-off ablation on the rungs where it
scored better, and the plain-mean centring of the constant-gauge variant.

the alternative it rejected. "What it would have bought" is the alternative's
gain on the in-distribution surface-pressure metric (float32, seed means)
where it had one; "what it reads" is the non-physical quantity the gain came
from; the evidence column points to the chapter or notebook entry that
carries the numbers and their artifacts.

: The design-decision ledger. Every number is stated in the chapter or notebook entry the row points to and carries its artifact there. {#tbl-principled-ledger}

Two rows deserve a sentence each, because they are the ones where the
principle cost the most.

**The measure weights** are the clearest case. With them, a slice state is
a quadrature estimate of a surface integral; without them it is a mean over
whichever points the mesher happened to place, and the network learns the
mesher. The price on the wings is real and understood: part of it is the
estimator variance of a quadrature-weighted mean over a heavy-tailed draw of
cell areas, which shrinks with cell count and is nearly gone at 40,000 cells
on the cars; the rest is mesh-pattern content in the ablation, which does
not shrink and which collapses the moment the sampling law changes. An
accuracy table at one cell count cannot tell these apart. The consistency
benchmark can, and it decided.

**The frame** is the case where the trade was closest, and it is stated
without softening. Where the same wings recur between training and
validation, an estimated centre and scale are worth 3 to 9% against the
frame-free construction, and at 210 recurring cases the similarity-gauge
variant met the accuracy condition this program had set for accepting it. It
was still declined, because the rungs that test geometries the model has
never seen favour the frame-free construction, and because an estimated
frame is a statistic of the sample even when it is a consistent one. For a
fixed fleet of shapes the gauge is the better instrument; the reference
configuration is built for the shapes that have not been seen yet.

## What we would ask of the field {#sec-principled-ask}

Three practices follow from the ledger, and none of them is expensive.

- **Measure consistency, not only accuracy.** Score every model under at
  least two sampling laws and at more than one cell count, and report
  whether the answers converge to each other. A model that is 10% better at
  10,000 cells and 10x worse under a different sampler has learned the mesher
  (@sec-consistency-bench).
- **Locate every gain before adopting it.** When a change improves the
  score, run the test that would reveal a discretization dependence, and ask
  what the change consumes that the physics does not supply. A mechanism that
  cannot be stated is a hypothesis; a gain whose mechanism is the mesh is not
  a gain.
- **Preregister the bar and keep the refuted configurations runnable.**
  Every decision above was made against a bar written before the run, and
  every rejected alternative remains runnable so that the price can be
  re-measured when the data or the metric change. The mainline class carries
  the reference configuration and the variants the chapters compare against
  (the constant and similarity gauges, the weights-off ablation, the interior
  modes); the falsified and diagnostic options were removed from it for
  integration into PhysicsNeMo and remain runnable, with their tests, at the
  git tag `isla-research-full` (@sec-program-status).

The accuracy metric is one number about one discretization of one dataset.
It is necessary and it is not sufficient, and a research program that
optimizes it alone will converge on surrogates that know their mesher better
than their physics.
